Championship|U19 World Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2007 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2007 Novi Sad]]|}} }} '''Hyland DeAndre Jordan Jr.''' (born July 21, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]]. Jordan was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the second round of the [[2008 NBA draft]] with the 35th overall pick. He spent ten seasons with the Clippers before signing with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in free agency in July 2018. He was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in January 2019 and joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in July of the same year. He was dealt to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in September 2021 and reached a contract buyout agreement before signing with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the same month. He was waived by the Lakers in March 2022 and subsequently joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He then signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]] in July 2022, with whom he won his first [[NBA championship]] in [[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]. Jordan is a three-time [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA]] and two-time [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] member, and has twice [[List of NBA annual rebounding leaders|led the NBA in rebounding]]. In 2017, he was named an [[NBA All-Star]] for the first time. {{As of|2025}}, Jordan holds the NBA record for highest career regular season and postseason [[field goal percentage]], at 67.4% and 67.0%, respectively.{{cite web |title=NBA & ABA Career Leaders and Records for Field Goal Pct |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leaders/fg_pct_career.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241206235627/https://www.basketball-reference.com/leaders/fg_pct_career.html |archive-date=December 6, 2024 |access-date=January 2, 2025 |website=[[Basketball Reference]] }} He is the Clippers' franchise leader in [[games played]], [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and [[Block (basketball)|blocks]]. He also won a [[gold medal]] at the [[2016 Summer Olympics]] as a member of the [[2016 United States men's Olympic basketball team|U.S. Olympic team]]. ==High school career== Jordan attended [[Episcopal High School (Bellaire, Texas)|Episcopal High School]] through his junior year. Jordan averaged 15.0 points, 12.0 rebounds, and 4.0 blocks as a sophomore; and 16.5 points, 14.0 rebounds, and 7.0 blocks as a junior. Jordan transferred to [[Christian Life Center Academy (Humble, Texas)|Christian Life Center Academy]] for his senior year, where he averaged 26.1 points, 15.2 rebounds, and 8.1 blocks per game. He was a third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], named to the first-team All-Greater Houston squad by the ''[[Houston Chronicle]]'' and was a two-time all-state selection. At Christian Life Center, Jordan posted a career-high 37 points in a game and also set the school record for most blocks in a game with 20. Coming out of high school, Jordan was rated as the number-eight overall prospect, the number-two center in the country, and the number-one prep player in Texas by [[Rivals.com]]. Jordan was recruited by Florida, Florida State, Indiana, Texas, Texas A&M, LSU, Kentucky, and others.[http://tamu.alliancesports.com/viewprospect.asp?Sport=2&pr_key=39241 DeAndre Jordan – Basketball Recruiting]. Tamu.alliancesports.com. In the summer of 2007, Jordan played for Team USA at the 2007 Under-19 World Championships in Serbia. Jordan played only nine minutes per game. Retrieved March 11, 2013. ==College career== Before Jordan arrived at [[Texas A&M University]] in [[College Station, Texas|College Station]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Aggies]] head basketball coach [[Billy Gillispie]] left the school to take the head coaching position at Kentucky. Jordan chose to honor his commitment to the university. Jordan started 21 of 35 games in his freshman season at Texas A&M. He averaged 20 minutes and 1.3 blocks per game. In those games, he shot a team-high of 61.7 percent in [[Field goal (basketball)|field goals]], but a team-low of 43.7 percent in [[free throws]]. Dallas News ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2008–2018)=== ====Early years (2008–2013)==== Jordan was selected with the 35th overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. Due to injuries among the Clippers low-post players, Jordan was pushed into the starting lineup for the January 19, 2009 game against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. In his first game as a starter, he recorded 8 points, 6 blocks and 10 rebounds in 34 minutes of play. In the January 21, 2009 game against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], he played 43 minutes and recorded a career-high 23 points. This included 10 dunks, which had only been accomplished by two others players ([[Dwight Howard]] and [[Shaquille O'Neal]]) over the past 10 NBA seasons.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/dailydime?page=dime-090126|title=Daily Dime: Bynum plays Duncan to a standstill – NBA – ESPN|access-date=October 16, 2016}}[[File:DeAndre Jordan 2.jpg|thumb|right|Jordan in 2011]] On December 11, 2011, Jordan signed an offer sheet with the [[Golden State Warriors]] reportedly worth $43 million over four years.{{cite web | title = Warriors Sign Center DeAndre Jordan To Offer Sheet | url = http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/deandre_jordan_offer_sheet.html | publisher = [[National Basketball Association]] | date = December 11, 2011 | access-date = December 13, 2011}} However, one day later, the Clippers matched the offer to keep him.{{cite web | title = CLIPPERS MATCH OFFER SHEET, RE-SIGN DEANDRE JORDAN | url = http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/transactions-111212.html | publisher = [[National Basketball Association]] | date = December 12, 2011 | access-date = December 13, 2011}} For the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]], Jordan changed his jersey number from 9 to 6.{{cite web | title = Great Expectations for DeAndre Jordan | url = http://www.nba.com/clippers/features/great-expectations-deandre-jordan-patten-111216.html | publisher = National Basketball Association | date = December 16, 2011 | access-date = December 20, 2011 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120108034142/http://www.nba.com/clippers/features/great-expectations-deandre-jordan-patten-111216.html | archive-date = January 8, 2012 | url-status = dead | df = mdy-all }} On December 25, 2011, Jordan recorded a career-high eight blocks against the Golden State Warriors in an opening day 105–86 victory. During the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]], Jordan's free-throw percentage dropped from 52.5% to 38.6%, one of his career worsts. However, he led the league in field-goal percentage, shooting 64.3%. This was his first season playing all 82 games. ====All-NBA and All-Defensive honors (2013–2016)==== [[File:DeAndre Jordan crop.jpg|thumb|upright|Jordan in 2013|left]] In 2013, Jordan was selected to Team USA's minicamp in Las Vegas.[http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/national/13_mnt_27players.html Twenty-Seven Players Confirmed For 2013 USA Basketball Men's National Team Mini-Camp] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130712064034/http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/national/13_mnt_27players.html |date=July 12, 2013 }} On November 29, 2013, Jordan recorded a career-high nine blocks in the 104–98 victory against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On January 3, 2014, Jordan scored a career-high 25 points in a 119–112 victory against the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. With 13.6 rebounds per game, he was the league's rebounding leader for the 2013–14 season. The team re-signed Aldridge on September 3.{{Cite web|title=Woj: DeAndre Jordan, 4 Picks Traded from Nets to Pistons for Okafor, Doumbouya|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2947888-woj-deandre-jordan-4-picks-traded-from-nets-to-pistons-for-okafor-doumbouya|url-status=live|access-date=November 20, 2021|website=Bleacher Report|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210903211921/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2947888-woj-deandre-jordan-4-picks-traded-from-nets-to-pistons-for-okafor-doumbouya |archive-date=September 3, 2021 }} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2021–2022)=== On September 3, 2021, Jordan was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Sekou Doumbouya]] and [[Jahlil Okafor]],{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Trade With Detroit Pistons|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/09/04/brooklyn-nets-complete-trade-detroit-pistons|website=NBA.com|date=September 4, 2021|access-date=September 4, 2021}} and he reached a buyout agreement with the team four days later.{{cite web|title=NBA Player Transactions|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/players/transactions|access-date=September 7, 2021}} On September 9, Jordan signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign DeAndre Jordan|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-deandre-jordan-2021|website=NBA.com|date=September 9, 2021|access-date=September 9, 2021}} On March 1, 2022, he was waived by the Lakers.{{Cite web |title=Lakers Sign D.J. This performance helped lead the injured Nuggets to a 113–104 win over his former team the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] alongside a fellow former Clipper having a breakout game, [[Reggie Jackson (basketball, born 1990)|Reggie Jackson]].{{cite web|title=DeAndre Jordan ESPN 2023-2024 Game Log|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3442/type/nba/year/2024|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 2, 2024}} On July 24, 2024, Jordan re-signed with the Nuggets.{{cite web|title=DENVER NUGGETS RE-SIGN DEANDRE JORDAN|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-re-sign-deandre-jordan-2|website=NBA.com|date=July 24, 2024|access-date=July 24, 2024}} He made 56 appearances (including five starts) for Denver during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 3.7 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 0.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=DeAndre Jordan 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3442/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=March 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2025–present)=== On October 24, 2025, Jordan signed a one-year, minimum-salary contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Pelicans Sign DeAndre Jordan To Strengthen Frontcourt Before Spurs Game|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-deandre-jordan-to-strengthen-frontcourt-before-spurs-game|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=October 24, 2025|access-date=October 24, 2025|last=Struck|first=Logan}} He made 12 appearances (including seven starts) for New Orleans during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 4.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 0.9 assists. Following the season, Jordan was named as the recipient of the Teammate of the Year award.{{Cite web|title=Pelicans' Jordan wins NBA's teammate of the year award|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48632377/pelicans-jordan-wins-nba-teammate-year-award|access-date=July 13, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On June 30, 2026, Jordan re-signed with the Pelicans on a one-year minimum contract.{{Cite web |last=Cohen |first=Eli |date=June 30, 2026 |title=DeAndre Jordan To Re-Sign With Pelicans |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2026/06/deandre-jordan-to-re-sign-with-pelicans.html |access-date=July 5, 2026 |website=HoopsRumors.com}} ==Personal life== Jordan is a Christian. Jordan prays frequently and has spoken about his faith saying, "I know my relationship with Christ, and I know what he has done for me, and that is what I live on."{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Clippers center Jordan presses forward with faith|url=http://www.thealabamabaptist.org/print-edition-article-detail.php?id_art=27639&pricat_art=9|access-date=February 10, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222032615/http://www.thealabamabaptist.org/print-edition-article-detail.php?id_art=27639&pricat_art=9|archive-date=February 22, 2014|url-status=dead}} Jordan has a tattoo of Matthew 5:4–5 on his chest,{{cite web|title=DeAndre Jordan's Ink| date=April 19, 2011 |url=http://dimemag.com/2011/04/deandre-jordans-ink/}} a Christian cross on his left arm,{{cite web|title=DeAndre Jordan's Ink| date=April 19, 2011 |url=http://dimemag.com/2011/04/deandre-jordans-ink/2/}} the [[Serenity Prayer]] and his own message saying "I thank God for the gift that he has given me. I will honor, sacrifice, and dedicate myself to my talent. I know where I have come from but I know where I am going" on his right arm,{{cite web|title=DeAndre Jordan's Ink| date=April 19, 2011 |url=http://dimemag.com/2011/04/deandre-jordans-ink/3/}}{{cite web|title=DeAndre Jordan's Ink| date=April 19, 2011 |url=http://dimemag.com/2011/04/deandre-jordans-ink/6/}} and Philippians 4:13 with praying hands and "G.W.O.M" (God Watch Over Me) on his stomach.{{cite web|title=DeAndre Jordan's Ink| date=April 19, 2011 |url=http://dimemag.com/2011/04/deandre-jordans-ink/5/}} Jordan is [[vegan]] for environmental reasons. He has hosted a vegan cooking show called ''Cooking Clean''.{{cite news |last1=Axworthy |first1=Nicole |title=NBA Star DeAndre Jordan Went Vegan "Cold Turkey" to Save the Planet |url=https://vegnews.com/2021/6/nba-star-deandre-jordan-went-vegan-to-save-the-planet |access-date=May 27, 2023 |work=VegNews.com}} Since 2020, Jordan has been enrolled in the Contemplative Studies program at [[Brown University]].[https://www.browndailyherald.com/article/2026/03/nba-player-deandre-jordan-discusses-practice-of-meditation-basketball NBA player DeAndre Jordan discusses practice of meditation, basketball] His younger brother, Avery Jordan, was a professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player in the [[Canadian Football League]].[https://www.foxsports.com/southwest/story/lowry-has-20-as-raptors-win-6th-straight-beat-mavs-116-107-2-102618 Lowry has 20 as Raptors win 6th straight, beat Mavs 116–107] ==Player profile== [[File:DeAndre Jordan free throw.jpg|thumb|Jordan, a regular recipient of the [[Hack-a-Shaq]] strategy, about to take a free throw in 2013.]] Jordan is a rebounder, averaging 10.2 rebounds per game in his career and leading the league in two seasons. He is also an post-defender averaging 1.5 blocks per game for his career.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jordade01.html|title=DeAndre Jordan Stats - Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=June 16, 2023}} Jordan's defensive play was a mix of tactics from [[Bill Russell]] focused on [[Block (basketball)|blocking shots]]. On offense, he heavily relies on put-backs and alley-oops to score. He did lead the league in field goal percentage for five seasons.{{cite web|url=http://www.rotoworld.com/articles/nba/50520/425/fanduel-nba-plays-monday|title=FanDuel NBA Plays: Monday|access-date=October 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064438/http://www.rotoworld.com/articles/nba/50520/425/fanduel-nba-plays-monday|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}} When it comes to being a free throw shooter, he makes just 47.5% of his shots at the line, leading to opponents exploiting this weakness by intentionally fouling him with the [[Hack-a-Shaq]] strategy.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/12817032/how-nba-get-rid-hack-shaq-method-nba|title=Pelton: How to get rid of Hack-a-Shaq| date=May 4, 2015 |access-date=October 16, 2016}} Jordan is considered one of the more durable players in the NBA, having played in 360 straight games at one point in his career.{{cite web |last=Turner |first=Broderick |date=April 14, 2014 |title=Whatever the lineup, DeAndre Jordan has a streak to consider |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-clippers-fyi-20140414-story.html |access-date=October 16, 2016
